text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 3 in history.

1014 - King Sweyn of Denmark I died and was succeeded by his son, Canute II the Great. After King Ethelred II of England ordered a massacre of Danes in 1002, Sweyn invaded Britain and conquered much of the country.
1194 - Henry VI of Germany released King Richard I (the Lion-Heart) of England, captured during the Third Crusade.
1399 - English Prince John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster, son of King Edward III and father of King Henry IV, died.
1807 - Montevideo was taken by British forces led by Sir Samuel Auchmuty.
1832 - English poet George Crabbe died; composer Benjamin Britten based his opera "Peter Grimes" on one of Crabbe's poems.
1867 - Prince Mutsuhito became Emperor Meiji of Japan at the age of 14 and reigned until 1912.
1913 - The 16th Amendment, or Income Tax Amendment, to the U.S. Constitution was ratified, authorising the power to impose and collect taxes on income.
1917 - The United States broke off diplomatic relations with Germany after Berlin announced a policy of unrestricted submarine warfare.
1919 - Kiev was captured by the Bolsheviks.
1919 - The first meeting of the League of Nations took place in Paris.
1924 - Woodrow Wilson, 28th president of the United States, died. His presidency was memorable for America's participation in World War One and his championship of the League of Nations.
1931 - A huge earthquake struck New Zealand, almost destroying the towns of Napier and Hastings.
1945 - U.S. aircraft dropped 3,000 tons of explosives on Berlin.
1954 - Queen Elizabeth II arrived in Australia for the first visit by a reigning monarch.
1958 - The Benelux Economic Union Treaty between Belgium, Luxembourg and Netherlands was signed.
1959 - Singers Buddy Holly, Richie Valens and the Big Bopper were killed in a plane crash in the United States.
1960 - British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan foreshadowed the decolonisation of Africa, telling the South African parliament: "The wind of change is blowing through the continent."
1966 - The first controlled landing on the moon was made by the Soviet unmanned spacecraft Luna IX.
1969 - The Palestine National Congress appointed Yasser Arafat head of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.

1977 - The chairman of the Provisional Military Government in Ethiopia, Brig-Gen Teferi Benti, and his closest associates were executed by supporters of the first vice-chairman, Lt-Col Mengistu Haile Mariam.
1978 - The European Economic Community and China initialled their first trade agreement.
1981 - Gro Harlem Brundtland was elected Norway's first woman prime minister following the resignation of Odvar Nordli.
1989 - John Cassavetes, U.S. actor and film-maker died; his appearances included "The Killers", "The DIrty Dozen" and "Rosemary's Baby".
1992 - Argentine President Carlos Menem signed a decree opening all files on Nazis who fled to South America after World War Two.
1994 - President Bill Clinton announced the lifting of the U.S. trade embargo against Vietnam, marking a dramatic shift in relations chilled for decades by war and postwar hostility.
1994 - The U.S. space shuttle Discovery blasted off, carrying five American astronauts and a Russian cosmonaut.
1994 - President Boris Yeltsin signed a treaty with Georgia reasserting Russia's military influence in the former Soviet republic.
1994 - The International Court of Justice, in a ruling on a 20-year border dispute, rejected Libya's claim to a huge swathe of neighbouring Chad's territory.
1996 - An earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale rocked southwestern China, killing at least 302 people and injuring 15,000.
1996 - Guinean President Lansana Conte reached agreement with the military to end a revolt sparked by a pay dispute.
